what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to accept the FY23 year-end encumbrance as proposed, carrying funds for cranes, manhole repairs, jetting and engineering into next year.
The Commission heard that a grease-related sewage backup occurred on Mass Ave the same day.
Commissioners were asked to send comments on a draft ARPA funding letter quickly; the final letter is due at the Select Board meeting on the 11th.
The maintenance contract for pump stations and generators will be rebid with the two combined and quantities reduced, while the current contract is extended two months.
Town counsel will be consulted on failed manhole concrete from the state repaving, and a second meeting was set for July 11.

why_it_matters: Sewer work is paid from user charges, which the business manager said are below projection, so carried-over spending and a rebid maintenance contract bear on what ratepayers are charged.
The grease backup and the manhole concrete from state repaving may lead to a changed grease trap policy or to repair costs, which would touch property owners on the sewer system.
watch_next: The July 11 Commission meeting, held before the joint selectmen's meeting.
The July 25 agenda, which is to include Wright-Pierce on flow redirection and an update on Pond View.
